title: San Diego with a dog: off-leash beaches, parks, patios and pet-friendly stays
excerpt: Where dogs can run off leash on the sand, the hours they can visit every other San Diego beach, which parks and trails allow them, and how to pick a pet-friendly rental.

seo.title: San Diego With a Dog: Beaches, Parks and Pet Rules 2026
seo.description: San Diego dog guide: off-leash beaches in Ocean Beach, Fiesta Island, Coronado and Del Mar, beach hours, dog parks, patio rules and pet-friendly stays.

heroCaption: The fenced patio at one of Cardo's pet-friendly homes in Ocean Beach, a short drive from Dog Beach.
bodyHtml:
San Diego is one of the easier places in California to travel with a dog, as long as you know which sand is open to them and at what hour. This guide covers the off-leash beaches, the time rules on the rest of the coast, the parks and trails that welcome dogs (and the ones that do not), how patio dining works under state law, and what to check before you book a pet-friendly stay. Rules are as of November 2026.

As of November 2026

Every rule below comes from the City of San Diego, the City of Coronado, the City of Del Mar, the National Park Service or California State Parks, linked where it appears. Cities do adjust hours and seasonal dates, so check the linked page before you go.

Where can dogs run off leash on the beach in San Diego?

Three beaches in the area allow dogs off leash year round: Dog Beach in Ocean Beach, the shoreline of Fiesta Island in Mission Bay, and Dog Beach in Coronado. Del Mar adds a fourth, North Beach, where dogs can run off leash for most of the year. Everywhere else on the City of San Diego coast, dogs are limited by the hour and must stay leashed.

Dog Beach, Ocean Beach

Dog Beach sits at the foot of Voltaire Street, where the San Diego River meets the ocean. The City lists it as a leash-free area open 24 hours, with access to both the sand and the surf. It is the best known of the three and the busiest on weekend mornings. Parking is in the lot at the end of Voltaire Street, and the Ocean Beach shops and cafes are a short walk south. The City's list of leash-free locations has the details.

Fiesta Island, Mission Bay

Fiesta Island is the larger option: the whole island is leash optional, shoreline and interior, with a 5.2-mile path around it for walkers. The City's leash-free list gives its hours as 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Two California least tern nesting sites stay fenced and locked all year, and two buffer zones close from April 15 to September 15. Dogs are also not allowed at the Youth Aquatic Center. The bay water is calm, which suits dogs that are new to swimming. See the City's dogs on beaches page.

Dog Beach, Coronado

Coronado's Dog Beach is at the north end of Ocean Boulevard, at 200 Ocean Boulevard. According to the City of Coronado, dogs may be off leash on the beach itself but must be leashed everywhere before it, including the path in. It pairs well with a day on the island; our Coronado neighborhood guide covers the rest.

North Beach, Del Mar

The City of Del Mar allows off-leash dogs between 29th Street and the Solana Beach border from the day after Labor Day through June 15. From June 16 through Labor Day, off-leash time on that stretch is limited to dawn to 8 a.m., and dogs must be leashed the rest of the day. South of 29th Street the rules are stricter: dogs must be leashed between Powerhouse Park and 29th Street most of the year and are banned there in summer. More on the town in our Del Mar guide.

Can I bring my dog to Pacific Beach, Mission Beach or La Jolla Shores?

Yes, but only early or late in the day, and on a leash. On City of San Diego beaches, the boardwalk and the parks next to them, dogs are not allowed from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. between November 1 and March 31, and from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. between April 1 and October 31. Outside those hours, dogs are welcome on a leash. Service animals are exempt.

In practice, that means a sunrise walk on the sand in Pacific Beach or a sunset loop on the Mission Beach boardwalk works well, while a midday beach day with the dog does not. The lifeguard beach regulations page lists the hours, and the same seasonal hours apply in most of Mission Bay Park outside Fiesta Island. Rangers, police, lifeguards and the San Diego Humane Society can all issue citations, and owners are expected to pick up after their dogs everywhere.

Which San Diego parks have off-leash areas for dogs?

The City lists about 20 leash-free parks. For visitors, the most useful are the ones near the coast and the central neighborhoods. In other City parks, dogs are allowed at any hour on a leash.

  • Nate's Point, Balboa Park: an open area on the south side of the Cabrillo Bridge, listed as open 24 hours. An easy add-on to a museum morning.
  • Morley Field, Balboa Park: open space northwest of the tennis courts, also 24 hours.
  • Capehart Park, Pacific Beach: a fenced one-acre park with separate pens for small and large dogs, water stations and parking, open 24 hours.
  • Dusty Rhodes Neighborhood Park, Ocean Beach: a one-acre area on Sunset Cliffs Boulevard, dawn to dusk.
  • Grape Street Park, South Park: off leash on Saturdays, Sundays and holidays from 9 a.m. to 9 p.m.

Are dogs allowed on San Diego hiking trails?

Some are, and two of the best known are not. Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve does not permit dogs anywhere in the reserve, according to California State Parks. At Cabrillo National Monument on Point Loma, the National Park Service allows pets only along the Coastal Trail, on a leash no longer than six feet; they are not allowed in the tidepools, on the Bayside Trail, at the lighthouse or visitor center, or along Cabrillo Road.

For a longer leashed walk with water views, the Fiesta Island path and the Mission Bay shoreline before 9 a.m. are reliable choices, and the Sunset Cliffs blufftop in Ocean Beach is a popular evening walk.

Can dogs eat on restaurant patios in San Diego?

Often, yes. California Health and Safety Code section 114259.5 lets a restaurant allow pet dogs in its outdoor dining area if the owner chooses to, the patio has its own outdoor entrance, and the dog stays on a leash or in a carrier and off chairs and benches. It is the restaurant's decision, not a right, so call ahead or ask at the host stand.

Ocean Beach, Pacific Beach, Liberty Station and North Park have many street-facing patios, and plenty of cafes put out water bowls. For more ideas on where to eat along the coast, see our guide to eating your way down the coast.

What should I check before booking a pet-friendly vacation rental?

Look at four things on the listing before you book: whether pets are allowed at all, how many dogs and what size, the pet fee, and whether the yard or patio is fenced. A fenced outdoor space matters more than it sounds, because it lets the dog settle in while you unpack and gives you an easy late-night stop.

Location is the other factor. If the plan is daily runs on the sand, a home in Ocean Beach puts Dog Beach within a walk or a short drive. If you would rather mix beach mornings with parks and patios, Pacific Beach, Point Loma and North Park are good bases.

As of November 13, 2026, Cardo manages 12 homes that accept pets, including three in Ocean Beach and others in Pacific Beach, La Jolla, Point Loma, Liberty Station, North Park and South Park. You can see them all with the pet-friendly filter on our booking site; each listing states its own pet rules and fees. Traveling with kids as well as a dog? Our guide to family days beyond the big parks has more ideas.

Quick reference

Off leash any time: Dog Beach (Ocean Beach), Coronado Dog Beach. Off leash, daytime hours: Fiesta Island. Off leash most of the year: Del Mar North Beach. Leashed and outside 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. (November to March) or 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. (April to October): all other City of San Diego beaches and boardwalks. No dogs: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve.
